why_how.text: At age sixteen or seventeen, Class D requires both DDS-approved driver education and the alcohol-and-drug-awareness program.

The approved driver-education course includes thirty classroom hours or an equivalent online course, together with six hours of certified on-road instruction or completion of the DDS parent-teen guide.
The Class D education requirement also includes at least forty hours of other driving experience, with at least six hours at night. A DDS affidavit signed at road testing certifies completion.
When a certified instructor provides the on-road driver-education component, a separate document confirming that component is required at the road test.
Without the required driver education, a teen cannot obtain Class D. The awareness program is available through many schools and online.
A teen whose parent is serving on active United States military duty may use an out-of-state driver-education certificate if it falls within nine months of the teen's sixteenth birthday.

why_how.text: A seventeen-year-old who documents military enlistment is exempt from the usual one-year-and-one-day learner-permit holding period; the handbook says this applicant receives Class C.
A Class D holder is prohibited from driving from midnight until five a.m.; the handbook states that this restriction has no exceptions.

During the first six months of Class D, passengers are restricted to immediate family, including parents, stepparents, grandparents, siblings, stepsiblings, children and anyone living at the driver's residence.
In the second six months of Class D, the vehicle may carry at most one passenger younger than twenty-one who is outside the driver's immediate family.
After the first twelve months of Class D, at most three passengers younger than twenty-one may be outside the driver's immediate family.
Before seeking Class C, a Class D holder must have no conviction during the preceding twelve months for a major traffic offense that mandates license suspension.

why_how.text: A new Georgia resident who wants to drive must apply for the Georgia license or permit within thirty days of establishing residency, subject to the handbook's stated exceptions.
A new resident without a valid out-of-state permit or license follows Georgia's first-issuance process, with the appropriate teen or adult requirements.

A transfer applicant younger than eighteen with a valid license or permit from another state or the District of Columbia normally qualifies for a comparable Georgia document only after meeting Georgia school, driver-education and awareness-program conditions.
For the adult state-to-state transfer route, the earlier license must be surrendered and must not have been expired for two years or more.
If an adult transfer applicant cannot surrender the earlier valid license, the handbook requires a certified driving history from the issuing state, dated within thirty days and showing valid status.
The regular transfer minimum is age eighteen. A seventeen-year-old may transfer an equivalent valid Class C license only when it has no restrictions on time, route, driving purpose or passengers.

An adult transfer applicant must provide the full Social Security number for verification, identity and citizenship or lawful-presence evidence, two Georgia residence documents, and pass a vision screening.

why_how.text: Transfer identity and lawful-presence documents must be originals or certified copies; a fax is not acceptable.
For a foreign credential missing from the applicant's possession, the handbook calls for an English-language driving history from the issuing country dated within the last thirty days.

Most noncitizens may keep a valid foreign driving or identification document after Georgia issues its equivalent. A United States citizen must surrender foreign-issued driving and identification credentials.

A document issued outside the United States states and the District of Columbia is generally processed as a new Georgia issuance, including the examinations applicable to the requested class and required identity, lawful-presence, Social Security and residence evidence.

Foreign-country applicants ordinarily complete knowledge, road and vision examinations; some countries have testing exemptions listed by DDS. The handbook does not identify those countries on this page.
Applicants younger than eighteen transferring from outside the country must also satisfy the additional teen-licensing requirements.
The handbook warns that privately operated sites may charge for information or training. It identifies the DDS government website as the official Georgia licensing source.
